title: web: Shiki CodeBlock SSR hydration mismatch on /showcase
description: The vendored CodeBlock (Shiki dual light/dark theme) emits inline color styles at SSR that differ from the client render, causing a React hydration mismatch warning when a CodeBlock is server-rendered (visible on /showcase via Tool input + Code Block cards). Cosmetic — React regenerates the subtree on the client and the page works. Proper fix lives in the vendored code-block.tsx (e.g. render code blocks client-only or suppressHydrationWarning on the pre/code). Same class of documented compromise as ignoreBuildErrors.
close_reason: Fixed Shiki CodeBlock SSR hydration mismatch. Root cause: highlightCode() reads a module-level tokensCache that lives for the whole Node process, so once the server highlights a block, later SSR renders emit COLORED tokens while every fresh client's first (hydration) render emits plain rawTokens (cold cache) -> React hydration mismatch (intermittent, depends on server cache warmth). Fix in code-block.tsx CodeBlockContent: added a mounted gate (useState(false)+useEffect setMounted(true)); tokenized = mounted ? (asyncTokens ?? syncTokens) : rawTokens. Forces SSR + client first render to both be rawTokens regardless of cache, then applies Shiki after mount. Verified live (agent-browser + curl): after warming server cache with 3+ SSR fetches, SSR HTML emits 0 server-side hex token colors (only color:inherit/transparent), console shows no hydration warnings, no page errors, and tokens highlight post-mount (real rgb color). typecheck 0, 63/63 vitest.
